questions.questionText: I think I ___ a mistake in the third answer.
questions.explanation: 'Make a mistake' is the fixed collocation; 'do a mistake' is wrong.

questions.questionText: Have you ___ your homework?
questions.explanation: 'Do homework' is the collocation; 'make homework' is incorrect.

questions.questionText: Please ___ attention to the instructions.
questions.explanation: The collocation is 'pay attention'.

questions.questionText: She ___ her promise and returned the money on time.
questions.explanation: 'Keep a promise' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: We ___ a lot of fun at the picnic.
questions.explanation: 'Have fun' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: Can you ___ a photo of us?
questions.explanation: 'Take a photo' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: There was ___ rain last night, and the streets flooded.
questions.explanation: Rain is described as 'heavy', not 'strong' or 'big'.

questions.questionText: He ___ a lie to avoid punishment.
questions.explanation: 'Tell a lie' is the fixed collocation.
questions.shortcut: Tell a lie / a story; say a word.

questions.questionText: You must ___ care of your health during the exams.
questions.explanation: 'Take care of' is the fixed expression.

questions.questionText: Shall I ___ some tea for you?
questions.explanation: 'Make tea' is the collocation; 'cook tea' is not used.

questions.questionText: Take a taxi to ___ time.
questions.explanation: 'Save time' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: Can you ___ a secret?
questions.explanation: 'Keep a secret' is the collocation.

questions.questionText: The baby was ___ asleep within minutes.
questions.explanation: 'Fast asleep' is a fixed collocation meaning deeply asleep.

questions.questionText: We must ___ an effort to reduce waste.
questions.explanation: 'Make an effort' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The government ___ a ban on plastic bags.
questions.explanation: 'Impose a ban' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: She drives a hard ___ with every supplier.
questions.explanation: 'Drive a hard bargain' is an idiom meaning to negotiate firmly.

questions.questionText: The minister ___ his resignation to the Prime Minister.
questions.explanation: 'Tender one's resignation' is the formal collocation.

questions.questionText: We should ___ a close watch on the situation.
questions.explanation: 'Keep a close watch' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The firm ___ heavy losses last year.
questions.explanation: Losses are 'incurred'; achieved, gained and won go with positive things.

questions.questionText: They ___ a warm welcome to the chief guest.
questions.explanation: 'Extend a welcome' is the formal collocation.

questions.questionText: It is time we ___ an end to this dispute.
questions.explanation: 'Put an end to' is the fixed expression.

questions.questionText: She ___ a deep sigh of relief.
questions.explanation: 'Heave a sigh' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: The detective ___ a blank when asked about the motive.
questions.explanation: 'Draw a blank' means to fail to find or recall anything.

questions.questionText: He was deep ___ debt after the business failed.
questions.explanation: 'Deep in debt' is the fixed collocation with 'in'.

questions.questionText: The passengers had a narrow ___ when the bus skidded.
questions.explanation: 'Narrow escape' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: It is an open ___ that he plans to retire.
questions.explanation: 'Open secret' means something known to everyone though officially secret.

questions.questionText: The patient is in ___ condition after the accident.
questions.explanation: A seriously ill patient is in 'critical condition'.

questions.questionText: He ___ his best to reach on time.
questions.explanation: 'Do one's best' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The thief was caught ___-handed.
questions.explanation: 'Caught red-handed' is the idiom.

questions.questionText: She ___ a complaint with the police.
questions.explanation: 'Lodge a complaint' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: The company ___ bankrupt after the scam.
questions.explanation: 'Go bankrupt' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The jury ___ the wrong conclusion from the evidence.
questions.explanation: 'Draw a conclusion' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: The rule is hard and ___; no exceptions are allowed.
questions.explanation: 'Hard and fast rules' is a fixed phrase.

questions.questionText: She was ___ with grief after her father's death.
questions.explanation: 'Overcome with grief' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: The accused was granted ___ on a bond of ₹50,000.
questions.explanation: Release pending trial against a bond is 'bail'.

questions.questionText: The chief minister laid the ___ stone of the hospital.
questions.explanation: 'Lay the foundation stone' is the fixed expression.

questions.questionText: The villagers turned a ___ ear to the officer's appeal.
questions.explanation: 'Turn a deaf ear' means to refuse to listen.

questions.questionText: The candidate ___ his election promise within a year of winning.
questions.explanation: 'Break a promise' is the collocation.

questions.questionText: The neighbours finally buried the ___ and became friends.
questions.explanation: 'Bury the hatchet' is the idiom for ending a quarrel.

questions.questionText: Lack of sleep can ___ havoc with your health.
questions.explanation: 'Play havoc with' is the fixed expression.

questions.questionText: She has a sweet ___ and cannot resist desserts.
questions.explanation: 'Sweet tooth' means a liking for sweet food.

questions.questionText: The speaker was given a standing ___ at the end.
questions.explanation: 'Standing ovation' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: The minister ___ the blame on the previous government.
questions.explanation: 'Lay the blame on' is the standard expression.

questions.questionText: The company ___ a profit of ₹5 crore this quarter.
questions.explanation: 'Make a profit' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: Do not take the matter ___; it is only a joke.
questions.explanation: 'Take lightly' is the standard collocation.

questions.questionText: He is a ___ sleeper and wakes at the slightest noise.
questions.explanation: 'Light sleeper' is the fixed collocation.

questions.questionText: Virat ___ the record for most centuries in the tournament.
questions.explanation: 'Break a record' is the collocation.

questions.questionText: Many small firms ___ business in this lane.
questions.explanation: 'Do business' is the collocation.

questions.questionText: Don't ___ your time on gossip.
questions.explanation: 'Waste time' is the collocation; 'pass time' means to occupy time and does not fit the warning.
